definition: The management of when each participant (user or AI system) should speak or respond during a conversation.
details: Turn-taking is a practical engineering concern in real-time conversational AI systems, particularly for voice interfaces, where the system must decide when a user has finished speaking and it is appropriate to respond.

explainer.lead: Turn-taking is the management of when each participant, user or AI system, should speak or respond in a conversation. It matters most in real-time voice interfaces, where responding too early or too late breaks the interaction.

tiers.eli5: It is knowing when it is your turn to talk and when to let the other person finish.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers implement end-of-speech detection and barge-in handling so the system waits for the user to finish before replying. A pitfall is misjudging pauses, causing the system to interrupt or stall.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally it is the policy deciding, at each point in a dialogue, whether the system should speak or yield, typically via end-of-turn detection over audio and context. Limit: no policy reliably separates thinking pauses from turn ends.

explainer.example: A voice assistant waits through a short silence, detects the user has finished, then responds without cutting them off.
